pamphlet_excerpts: Overhead Line Hazards: Check the casting zone for overhead power lines before making any cast.
Eye Protection Gear: Wear impact resistant sunglasses to protect eyes from errant hooks and weights.
Deep Wading Protocol: Fasten a secure wading belt around waders to prevent catastrophic water flooding.
Lightning Strike Safety: Exit the water immediately when distant thunder rumbles across open waterways.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Perimeter Scan: Survey the bank for loose gravel, slippery mud, and overhead utility lines.
Step 2 - Gear Preparation: Don polarized safety glasses and secure an approved life jacket before casting.
Step 3 - Distance Check: Maintain at least one rod length of clearance between all neighboring anglers.
Step 4 - Hook Securing: Fasten the exposed hook to the rod keeper ring during trail travel.
gear_checklist: Balanced rod, reel, monofilament/fluorocarbon line, leaders, and barbless or circle hooks.
Needle-nose pliers/hemostat for safe hook removal, line clippers, and polarized eye protection.
Arbor knot, clinch knot, and blood/surgeon's knot practice cord and state fishing regulations guide.
U.S. Coast Guard-approved Type III PFD (when wading or boating) and first-aid kit.

misconception_pool.misconception: Pulling a barbed fishhook straight backward out of a finger causes less tissue damage than using the string-yank technique.
misconception_pool.fact: Pulling a barbed hook backward shreds flesh as the barb catches; depressing the shank disengages the barb along the entry path.

misconception_pool.misconception: Any embedded fishhook can be safely removed in the field by advancing the point through the skin and clipping the barb.
misconception_pool.fact: Hooks embedded near the face, eyes, tendons, or major blood vessels must be stabilized in place and removed only by a physician.

misconception_pool.misconception: Wading in cool spring trout streams poses no hypothermia risk as long as the air temperature remains above seventy degrees.
misconception_pool.fact: Water conducts heat away from the body twenty-five times faster than air, causing hypothermia even on warm, sunny afternoons.

misconception_pool.misconception: Puncture wounds from catfish pectoral spines bleed freely enough to flush out bacteria without needing soap and clean water.
misconception_pool.fact: Narrow puncture wounds trap aquatic bacteria and venom deep in tissue, requiring thorough irrigation with clean water and soap.

misconception_pool.misconception: Tightly locked drag systems preserve reel springs and internal washers during winter storage.
misconception_pool.fact: Storing reels with tight drag compresses felt washers and permanently ruins smooth drag operation.

misconception_pool.misconception: Blasting a saltwater fishing reel with a pressurized garden hose is the best way to flush salt out of the gear housing.
misconception_pool.fact: High-pressure water drives salt crystals and grit past outer seals into the bearings; use a gentle mist or damp cloth instead.

misconception_pool.misconception: Tightening the star drag or front drag knob all the way down before storing a reel preserves the tension spring alignment.
misconception_pool.fact: Leaving the drag tightened during storage permanently compresses the internal drag washers, causing jerky line release later.

misconception_pool.misconception: Fly rods and spinning rods cast by using the weight of the terminal lure to pull line directly off the reel spool.
misconception_pool.fact: Spinning outfits use lure weight to pull thin line off a fixed spool, whereas fly fishing uses heavy coated line to carry a fly.

misconception_pool.misconception: Hooking a treble lure directly through the ceramic insert of a rod guide protects the blank while walking along a trail.
misconception_pool.fact: Metal hooks scratch and crack fragile ceramic guide inserts, which then slice fishing line; secure hooks to the hook keeper.

pamphlet_excerpts: Knife Blade Sharpness: Maintain a razor sharp flexible blade to slice meat cleanly without tearing flesh.
Entrail Removal Protocol: Slice along the belly slit without puncturing internal organs or the bitter gall bladder.
